title: Strict transform comparison after multiplying a center by a Cartier divisor
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose defining ideal $\mathcal I_Z$ is finite-type quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and let $D\subseteq S$ be an effective Cartier divisor, i.e. a closed subscheme whose ideal $\mathcal I_D$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Let $Z_D\subseteq S$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_D$, let $b:S'\to S$ be the blow-up in $Z$ and $b_D:S'_D\to S$ the blow-up in $Z_D$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and fix the isomorphism $\varphi:S'_D\cong S'$ over $S$ of [lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor]. For every morphism $f:X\to S$ [def-pc-scheme] and quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] having no nonzero local sections supported on $f^{-1}(D)$, the module strict transform of $\mathcal F$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform] relative to the centre $Z$, a quotient of the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X\times_S S'$, and its module strict transform relative to the centre $Z_D$, a quotient of the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X\times_S S'_D$, correspond under $\mathrm{id}_X\times_S\varphi$ [def-pc-fibre-product]: the two quotients of the pullback of $\mathcal F$ have the same kernel.

source.place: Tag 080H, divisors-lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, clause (2); the identification of the two blow-ups is clause (1), carried by lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible] the effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D$ is invertible, so [lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor] applies to $\mathcal L=\mathcal I_D$, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I_Z$ and gives the fixed isomorphism $\varphi:S'_D\cong S'$ over $S$, i.e. $b\circ\varphi=b_D$. Hence $\mathrm{id}_X\times_S\varphi:X\times_SS'_D\to X\times_SS'$ is an isomorphism commuting with the projections to $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and it carries the pullback of $\mathcal F$ on the one side to the pullback on the other. The centre ideal $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_D$ is of finite type (locally generated by the products of finitely many generators of $\mathcal I_Z$ with one generator of $\mathcal I_D$), so both module strict transforms are defined [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Because $\varphi$ is over $S$, it maps $b_D^{-1}V(\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_D)=b_D^{-1}(Z\cup D)$ onto $b^{-1}(Z\cup D)$. So, by the definition [def-trf-module-strict-transform], after transport by $\mathrm{id}_X\times_S\varphi$ the two kernels are, inside $p^*\mathcal F$ on $X\times_SS'$: $\mathcal K$, the local sections vanishing off $q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z)$, and $\mathcal K_D$, the local sections vanishing off $q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z\cup D)$. It remains to show $\mathcal K=\mathcal K_D$. Both are quasi-coherent submodules of $p^*\mathcal F$ by [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] (applied to the centres $Z$ and $Z_D$).

source.place: Tag 080H, clause (1) and the opening of the proof of clause (2).

proof.text: Equality of two quasi-coherent submodules can be checked on an affine open cover, so we compute on charts. Cover $S$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ on which $\mathcal I_D=(x)$ with $x\in A$ a nonzerodivisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] and $\mathcal I_Z$ corresponds to a finitely generated ideal $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$ (finite type, [pqf-def-coherent]). Over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ the blow-up $S'$ is covered by the charts $\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/f_i])$ [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Fix $a=f_i$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\subseteq f^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $\mathcal F|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}=\widetilde M$. Then $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/a])=\operatorname{Spec}(C_a(A,R,I))$ [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring], and these $W$ cover $X\times_SS'$; on $W$ the pullback is $p^*\mathcal F|_W=\widetilde N$ with $N=M\otimes_R(R\otimes_AA[I/a])=M\otimes_AA[I/a]$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Elementary: since $f=a\cdot(f/a)$ for $f\in I$ and $a\in I$, $IA[I/a]=aA[I/a]$, so $W\cap q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z)=V(a)$ and $W\cap q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z\cup D)=V(xa)$; and since $\widetilde N(D(r))=N_r$, a section $s\in N$ restricts to zero on $D(r)$ iff $r^ns=0$ for some $n$ (Tag 01I8). Hence the global sections over $W$ of the quasi-coherent submodules $\mathcal K|_W$ and $\mathcal K_D|_W$ are $\Gamma_{(a)}(N)$ and $\Gamma_{(xa)}(N)$ [def-nagata-power-torsion], and $\mathcal K|_W=\Gamma_{(a)}(N)^\sim$, $\mathcal K_D|_W=\Gamma_{(xa)}(N)^\sim$.

source.place: Tag 080H, proof of clause (2), sentence 'Using Lemma 080G the second statement translates into the following algebra problem'; Tag 080G (lemma-blowing-up-affine) for the chart cover.

proof.text: An element $m\in M$ with $x^nm=0$ is a section of $\mathcal F$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ vanishing on $D(x)$, i.e. supported on $f^{-1}(D)\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$; by hypothesis it is zero. So $\Gamma_{(x)}(M)=0$ for $M$ regarded as an $A$-module, and $x$ is a nonzerodivisor of $A$. The affine torsion comparison [lem-trf-strict-transform-affine-torsion-comparison] gives $\Gamma_{(a)}(M\otimes_AA[I/a])=\Gamma_{(xa)}(M\otimes_AA[I/a])$, so $\mathcal K|_W=\mathcal K_D|_W$ by step 2.

source.place: Tag 080H, algebra reduction paragraph and final sentence of the proof of clause (2).

proof.text: The opens $W$ of step 2 cover $X\times_SS'$, so the subsheaves $\mathcal K$ and $\mathcal K_D$ of $p^*\mathcal F$ agree. Transporting back along the isomorphism $\mathrm{id}_X\times_S\varphi$ of step 1, the two quotient maps of the pullback of $\mathcal F$ defining the module strict transforms relative to $Z$ and to $Z_D$ have the same kernel.

proof_origin.place: Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, clause (2), proof via the affine torsion calculation.
